title: Customer reviews and how a day is judged
summary: A day in TCG Card Shop Simulator leaves an impression: the game defines customer reviews with their own data, screen, panel and even the text customers use.
body: Reviews are recorded by the game, which is why a bad day has consequences beyond the till rather than being forgotten.
The text of a review comes from the game's own table of lines, so what a customer says is drawn from data rather than generated on the fly.
A review on that panel is made of parts. It carries the text of the review, the time it was left and a list of stars, so a rating is drawn from data rather than written into the panel.
There is a screen and a panel for reviews, which means looking them up is something you can do deliberately rather than wait to be told.
What this entry does not tell you: how reviews affect customers or how many you need to recover a reputation. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Customer reviews are managed by the game.
Reviews have their own screen and panel.
The wording of a review comes from a data table.
Waiting customers are removed from a queue by the game's own handling.
A review panel shows the review text, the time it was left and a list of star images.
